items.stem: What is meant by “glycocalyx”?
items.answer: The outermost layer of the bacterial cell envelope, which may be a loose slime layer or a thick, tough capsule.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: the outermost layer of the bacterial cell envelope, which may be a loose slime layer or a thick, tough capsule.

items.stem: Classify each of the following as surface structure of bacteria or inclusion body: gas vacuoles, fimbriae, flagella, glycogen granules.
items.answer: gas vacuoles – inclusion body; fimbriae – surface structure of bacteria; flagella – surface structure of bacteria; glycogen granules – inclusion body.
items.markingKey: ½ mark each: gas vacuoles – inclusion body; fimbriae – surface structure of bacteria; flagella – surface structure of bacteria; glycogen granules – inclusion body.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): Schleiden and Schwann explained how new cells are formed.
Reason (R): Ribosomes of prokaryotes are 70S.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: A is false, but R is true.
items.markingKey: (d) A is false: Their cell theory did not explain how new cells form; Virchow modified it. R is a true statement.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: The following statement is incorrect. Rewrite it correctly and give a reason: “Prokaryotes have a well-defined nucleus.”
items.answer: Prokaryotes have a nucleoid without a nuclear membrane.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the corrected statement, 1 mark for the reason: Prokaryotes have a nucleoid without a nuclear membrane.

items.stem: Give two differences between a eukaryotic cell and a prokaryotic cell.
items.answer: A eukaryotic cell: genetic material organised into chromosomes; 80S ribosomes in the cytoplasm. A prokaryotic cell: no well-defined nucleus; nucleoid present; 70S ribosomes.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for each correct, paired difference, e.g. a eukaryotic cell – genetic material organised into chromosomes; 80S ribosomes in the cytoplasm; a prokaryotic cell – no well-defined nucleus; nucleoid present; 70S ribosomes.

items.stem:
A microbiology student in Pune stained two bacteria. One retained the purple stain; the other did not.
(i) Name the staining technique. (1 mark)
(ii) What are the two groups called? (1 mark)
(iii) The bacterial envelope has three layers. Name them and the function of the outermost. (2 marks)
items.answer: (i) Gram staining. (ii) Gram positive (retain stain) and Gram negative. (iii) Glycocalyx, cell wall, plasma membrane; glycocalyx (slime layer or capsule) protects the cell.

items.stem:
(a) Distinguish between a prokaryotic cell and a eukaryotic cell on any three points. (3 marks)
(b) A cell has these features: no membrane-bound organelles. Identify the type of cell – a prokaryotic cell or a eukaryotic cell? Justify your answer. (2 marks)
items.answer: (a) A prokaryotic cell: no well-defined nucleus; nucleoid present; no membrane-bound organelles; 70S ribosomes. A eukaryotic cell: well-defined nucleus with nuclear envelope; membrane-bound organelles present; 80S ribosomes in the cytoplasm. (b) A prokaryotic cell.
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark for each of three paired differences. (b) 1 mark: a prokaryotic cell; 1 mark: “no membrane-bound organelles” is a feature of a prokaryotic cell.

items.stem: A cell has these features: well-defined nucleus with nuclear envelope; 80S ribosomes in the cytoplasm; membrane-bound organelles present. Identify the type of cell. Give a reason.
items.answer: A eukaryotic cell
items.markingKey: 1 mark: a eukaryotic cell; 1 mark: the features well-defined nucleus with nuclear envelope; 80S ribosomes in the cytoplasm; membrane-bound organelles present are characteristic of it.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about the cell theory and prokaryotic cells is correct?
items.answer: Rudolf Virchow (1855) explained that cells divide and new cells are formed from pre-existing cells (Omnis cellula-e cellula).
items.markingKey: (a) Rudolf Virchow (1855) explained that cells divide and new cells are formed from pre-existing cells (Omnis cellula-e cellula). The other statements are false. Their cell theory did not explain how new cells form; Virchow modified it. Prokaryotic ribosomes are 70S, made of 50S and 30S subunits. Prokaryotes have a nucleoid without a nuclear membrane.
options: Rudolf Virchow (1855) explained that cells divide and new cells are formed from pre-existing cells (Omnis cellula-e cellula).
Schleiden and Schwann explained how new cells are formed.

items.stem:
(a) Distinguish between a prokaryotic cell and a eukaryotic cell on any three points. (3 marks)
(b) A cell has these features: may have plasmids and mesosomes. Identify the type of cell – a prokaryotic cell or a eukaryotic cell? Justify your answer. (2 marks)
items.answer: (a) A prokaryotic cell: no well-defined nucleus; nucleoid present; no membrane-bound organelles; 70S ribosomes. A eukaryotic cell: well-defined nucleus with nuclear envelope; membrane-bound organelles present; 80S ribosomes in the cytoplasm. (b) A prokaryotic cell.
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark for each of three paired differences. (b) 1 mark: a prokaryotic cell; 1 mark: “may have plasmids and mesosomes” is a feature of a prokaryotic cell.

items.stem: State the cell theory and its modification. Describe the structure of a typical prokaryotic cell with a labelled diagram.
items.answer: Schleiden and Schwann: all living organisms are composed of cells and products of cells; Virchow: all cells arise from pre-existing cells. Prokaryote: cell envelope – glycocalyx, cell wall, plasma membrane; mesosomes; nucleoid with naked circular DNA; plasmids; 70S ribosomes, polysomes; inclusion bodies; flagella, pili, fimbriae.
items.markingKey: 1 mark cell theory; 4 marks structure with diagram.

items.stem: Define the term “active transport”.
items.answer: Movement of molecules across the membrane against the concentration gradient using energy from ATP, as in the Na⁺/K⁺ pump.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: movement of molecules across the membrane against the concentration gradient using energy from ATP, as in the Na⁺/K⁺ pump.

items.stem: Classify each of the following as component of the endomembrane system or organelle not part of the endomembrane system: chloroplasts, peroxisomes, lysosomes, vacuoles.
items.answer: chloroplasts – organelle not part of the endomembrane system; peroxisomes – organelle not part of the endomembrane system; lysosomes – component of the endomembrane system; vacuoles – component of the endomembrane system.
items.markingKey: ½ mark each: chloroplasts – organelle not part of the endomembrane system; peroxisomes – organelle not part of the endomembrane system; lysosomes – component of the endomembrane system; vacuoles – component of the endomembrane system.

items.stem: Which of the following is NOT an organelle not part of the endomembrane system?
items.answer: lysosomes
items.markingKey: (a) Lysosomes is a component of the endomembrane system, not an organelle not part of the endomembrane system.

items.stem: The following statement is incorrect. Rewrite it correctly and give a reason: “In the fluid mosaic model, proteins are fixed and cannot move.”
items.answer: The quasi-fluid lipid allows lateral movement of proteins within the bilayer.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the corrected statement, 1 mark for the reason: The quasi-fluid lipid allows lateral movement of proteins within the bilayer.

items.stem: A cell organelle has these features: major site for synthesis of lipids; part of the endomembrane system. Identify the organelle.
items.answer: the smooth endoplasmic reticulum
items.markingKey: (c) The smooth endoplasmic reticulum: major site for synthesis of lipids; part of the endomembrane system.

items.stem: What is the endomembrane system? Name its components and explain why mitochondria are not included.
items.answer: A group of membranous organelles whose functions are coordinated: endoplasmic reticulum, Golgi complex, lysosomes and vacuoles. Mitochondria, chloroplasts and peroxisomes are excluded because their functions are not coordinated with these components.
items.markingKey: 1 mark definition; 1 mark components; 1 mark reason.

items.stem:
Fatima studied cells of a pancreas that secrete large amounts of digestive enzymes. Under the electron microscope she saw membranes studded with granules and many stacks of flattened sacs near the nucleus.
(i) Name the membranes studded with granules. (1 mark)
(ii) Name the stacks of flattened sacs. (1 mark)
(iii) Explain how these two organelles work together in enzyme secretion. (2 marks)
items.answer: (i) Rough endoplasmic reticulum. (ii) Golgi apparatus (cisternae). (iii) Proteins are synthesised by ribosomes on RER and move in vesicles to the cis face of the Golgi; they are modified and packaged and leave from the trans face as secretory vesicles.

items.stem:
(a) Distinguish between the vacuole and the rough endoplasmic reticulum on any three points. (3 marks)
(b) A cell organelle has these features: continuous with the outer nuclear membrane. Identify the organelle – the vacuole or the rough endoplasmic reticulum? Justify your answer. (2 marks)
items.answer: (a) The vacuole: membrane-bound space in the cytoplasm; bound by a single membrane called the tonoplast; contains water, sap, excretory products. The rough endoplasmic reticulum: network of tubules with ribosomes on its outer surface; frequently observed in cells active in protein synthesis and secretion; continuous with the outer nuclear membrane. (b) The rough endoplasmic reticulum.
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark for each of three paired differences. (b) 1 mark: the rough endoplasmic reticulum; 1 mark: “continuous with the outer nuclear membrane” is a feature of the rough endoplasmic reticulum.

items.stem: A cell organelle has these features: bound by a single membrane called the tonoplast; membrane-bound space in the cytoplasm. Identify the organelle. Give a reason.
items.answer: The vacuole
items.markingKey: 1 mark: the vacuole; 1 mark: the features bound by a single membrane called the tonoplast; membrane-bound space in the cytoplasm are characteristic of it.

items.stem: Which term describes flat, disc-shaped sacs of the Golgi apparatus, stacked parallel to each other?
items.answer: cisternae
items.markingKey: (b) Cisternae: flat, disc-shaped sacs of the Golgi apparatus, stacked parallel to each other.

items.stem:
(a) Distinguish between the smooth endoplasmic reticulum and the Golgi apparatus on any three points. (3 marks)
(b) A cell organelle has these features: packages materials for intracellular targets or secretion. Identify the organelle – the smooth endoplasmic reticulum or the Golgi apparatus? Justify your answer. (2 marks)
items.answer: (a) The smooth endoplasmic reticulum: no ribosomes on its surface; major site for synthesis of lipids; synthesises steroidal hormones in animal cells. The Golgi apparatus: stacks of flat, disc-shaped cisternae; cis (forming) and trans (maturing) faces; packages materials for intracellular targets or secretion. (b) The Golgi apparatus.
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark for each of three paired differences. (b) 1 mark: the Golgi apparatus; 1 mark: “packages materials for intracellular targets or secretion” is a feature of the Golgi apparatus.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about the cell membrane, cell wall and endomembrane system is correct?
items.answer: In plant cells the vacuole can occupy up to 90 per cent of the volume of the cell.
items.markingKey: (c) In plant cells the vacuole can occupy up to 90 per cent of the volume of the cell. The other statements are false. Smooth ER synthesises lipids; rough ER, with ribosomes, synthesises and secretes proteins. Lysosomal hydrolases are optimally active at acidic pH. Mitochondria, chloroplasts and peroxisomes are not part of it because their functions are not coordinated with ER, Golgi, lysosomes and vacuoles.
options: Mitochondria are part of the endomembrane system.
Rough ER is the main site of lipid synthesis.
In plant cells the vacuole can occupy up to 90 per cent of the volume of the cell.
Lysosomal enzymes are active at alkaline pH.

items.stem: Distinguish between lysosomes and the Golgi apparatus on any three points.
items.answer: Lysosomes: enzymes optimally active at acidic pH; formed by packaging in the Golgi apparatus; membrane-bound vesicular structures. The Golgi apparatus: site of formation of glycoproteins and glycolipids; packages materials for intracellular targets or secretion; cis (forming) and trans (maturing) faces.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for each of three correct, paired points of difference, e.g. lysosomes – enzymes optimally active at acidic pH; formed by packaging in the Golgi apparatus; membrane-bound vesicular structures; the Golgi apparatus – site of formation of glycoproteins and glycolipids; packages materials for intracellular targets or secretion; cis (forming) and trans (maturing) faces.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): Rough ER is abundant in cells that secrete lipids.

items.answer: A is false, but R is true.
items.markingKey: (d) Rough ER is abundant in protein-secreting cells; R is true.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: Define the term “nucleolus”.
items.answer: A spherical structure in the nucleus that is the site of active ribosomal RNA synthesis.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: a spherical structure in the nucleus that is the site of active ribosomal RNA synthesis.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about mitochondria, plastids, ribosomes, the cytoskeleton, cilia, centrosome and the nucleus is correct?
items.answer: Mitochondria divide by fission.
items.markingKey: (c) Mitochondria divide by fission. The other statements are false. The inner membrane forms cristae. The nucleolus is not membrane bound; its contents are continuous with the nucleoplasm. Mature RBCs of many mammals and sieve tube cells of vascular plants lack a nucleus.
options: The outer mitochondrial membrane forms cristae.
Nucleoli are bound by a membrane.
Mature mammalian RBCs have a nucleus.

items.stem: Which of the following is NOT a double-membrane-bound organelle?
items.answer: vacuole
items.markingKey: (a) Vacuole is a single-membrane-bound organelle, not a double-membrane-bound organelle.

items.answer: The ribosome
items.markingKey: 1 mark: the ribosome; 1 mark: the features site of protein synthesis; granular structure without a membrane; 70S in prokaryotes and 80S in eukaryotes are characteristic of it.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): Centrioles are found in both plant and animal cells.

options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.markingKey: (d) The chloroplast: double membrane; thylakoids stacked as grana in the stroma.

(ii) State one more feature you would expect to observe. (1 mark)
(iii) How would the observations differ if it were the mitochondrion? Give two points. (2 marks)
items.answer: (i) The chloroplast (ii) traps light energy for photosynthesis (iii) divides by fission; matrix with circular DNA and 70S ribosomes
items.markingKey: (i) the chloroplast – 1 mark. (ii) any one of: traps light energy for photosynthesis – 1 mark. (iii) for the mitochondrion: double membrane, inner one folded into cristae; matrix with circular DNA and 70S ribosomes; site of aerobic respiration – 1 mark each for any two.

items.stem:
(a) Distinguish between the ribosome and the centrosome on any three points. (3 marks)
(b) A cell organelle has these features: site of protein synthesis. Identify the organelle – the ribosome or the centrosome? Justify your answer. (2 marks)
items.answer: (a) The ribosome: granular structure without a membrane; made of RNA and proteins; 70S in prokaryotes and 80S in eukaryotes. The centrosome: contains two cylindrical centrioles; centrioles lie perpendicular to each other; each centriole has nine peripheral triplet fibrils. (b) The ribosome.
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark for each of three paired differences. (b) 1 mark: the ribosome; 1 mark: “site of protein synthesis” is a feature of the ribosome.

items.stem: Name three types of plastids with the pigments or materials they contain.

items.markingKey: ½ mark each: lysosome – single-membrane-bound organelle; centriole – non-membrane-bound organelle; microtubule – non-membrane-bound organelle; ribosome – non-membrane-bound organelle.

items.stem: Explain the term “peroxisomes”.
items.answer: Microbodies containing enzymes that take part in photorespiration in plants and break down hydrogen peroxide.

items.markingKey: (i) the vacuole – 1 mark. (ii) any one of: membrane-bound space in the cytoplasm – 1 mark. (iii) for lysosomes: membrane-bound vesicular structures; formed by packaging in the Golgi apparatus; rich in hydrolytic enzymes – 1 mark each for any two.

items.stem: A cell has these features: no plastids; centrioles present. Identify the type of cell. Give a reason.
items.answer: An animal cell
items.markingKey: 1 mark: an animal cell; 1 mark: the features no plastids; centrioles present are characteristic of it.

items.stem:

Reason (R): Nucleoli are bound by a membrane.

items.answer: A is true, but R is false.
items.markingKey: (c) A is true. R is false: The nucleolus is not membrane bound; its contents are continuous with the nucleoplasm.

items.stem: A cell has these features: genetic material organised into chromosomes; membrane-bound organelles present; 80S ribosomes in the cytoplasm. Identify the type of cell. Give a reason.
items.answer: A eukaryotic cell

items.stem:
(a) Distinguish between the smooth endoplasmic reticulum and the rough endoplasmic reticulum on any three points. (3 marks)
(b) A cell organelle has these features: synthesises steroidal hormones in animal cells. Identify the organelle – the smooth endoplasmic reticulum or the rough endoplasmic reticulum? Justify your answer. (2 marks)
items.answer: (a) The smooth endoplasmic reticulum: no ribosomes on its surface; major site for synthesis of lipids; synthesises steroidal hormones in animal cells. The rough endoplasmic reticulum: network of tubules with ribosomes on its outer surface; frequently observed in cells active in protein synthesis and secretion; continuous with the outer nuclear membrane. (b) The smooth endoplasmic reticulum.
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark for each of three paired differences. (b) 1 mark: the smooth endoplasmic reticulum; 1 mark: “synthesises steroidal hormones in animal cells” is a feature of the smooth endoplasmic reticulum.

items.stem: What is meant by “central vacuole”?
items.answer: A large vacuole of a mature plant cell bounded by the tonoplast.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: a large vacuole of a mature plant cell bounded by the tonoplast.

items.stem: Which of the following is NOT a surface structure of bacteria?
items.answer: cyanophycean granules
items.markingKey: (d) Cyanophycean granules is an inclusion body, not a surface structure of bacteria.

items.stem: Give two differences between the mitochondrion and the ribosome.
items.answer: The mitochondrion: double membrane, inner one folded into cristae; divides by fission. The ribosome: 70S in prokaryotes and 80S in eukaryotes; made of RNA and proteins.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for each correct, paired difference, e.g. the mitochondrion – double membrane, inner one folded into cristae; divides by fission; the ribosome – 70S in prokaryotes and 80S in eukaryotes; made of RNA and proteins.

items.stem:
(a) Distinguish between an animal cell and a plant cell on any three points. (3 marks)
(b) A cell has these features: plastids present. Identify the type of cell – an animal cell or a plant cell? Justify your answer. (2 marks)
items.answer: (a) An animal cell: no cell wall; no plastids; vacuoles small or absent. A plant cell: cell wall of cellulose present; plastids present; large central vacuole. (b) A plant cell.
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark for each of three paired differences. (b) 1 mark: a plant cell; 1 mark: “plastids present” is a feature of a plant cell.

items.stem: The following statement is incorrect. Rewrite it correctly and give a reason: “Schleiden and Schwann explained how new cells are formed.”
items.answer: Their cell theory did not explain how new cells form; Virchow modified it.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the corrected statement, 1 mark for the reason: Their cell theory did not explain how new cells form; Virchow modified it.

items.stem: Which of the following is a component of the endomembrane system?
items.answer: endoplasmic reticulum
items.markingKey: (b) Endoplasmic reticulum is a component of the endomembrane system; the others are not.

items.stem: Explain the term “cytoskeleton”.
items.answer: An elaborate network of filamentous proteinaceous structures in the cytoplasm made of microtubules, microfilaments and intermediate filaments.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: an elaborate network of filamentous proteinaceous structures in the cytoplasm made of microtubules, microfilaments and intermediate filaments.

items.stem: Give two differences between the rough endoplasmic reticulum and the vacuole.
items.answer: The rough endoplasmic reticulum: network of tubules with ribosomes on its outer surface; continuous with the outer nuclear membrane. The vacuole: may occupy up to 90% of a plant cell; bound by a single membrane called the tonoplast.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for each correct, paired difference, e.g. the rough endoplasmic reticulum – network of tubules with ribosomes on its outer surface; continuous with the outer nuclear membrane; the vacuole – may occupy up to 90% of a plant cell; bound by a single membrane called the tonoplast.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about microbodies and the differences between plant and animal cells is correct?
items.answer: Both plant and animal cells have mitochondria and Golgi apparatus.
items.markingKey: (a) Both plant and animal cells have mitochondria and Golgi apparatus. The other statements are false. Animal cells have small vacuoles or none; plant cells have a large central vacuole. Animal cells have centrioles; they are absent in almost all plant cells. Animal cells lack a cell wall.

Animal cells have a large central vacuole.
Animal cells have a cellulose cell wall.
Plant cells have centrioles but animal cells do not.

items.stem: Give three differences between the centrosome and the nucleus.
items.answer: The centrosome: contains two cylindrical centrioles; each centriole has nine peripheral triplet fibrils; forms spindle apparatus in animal cells. The nucleus: contains nucleoplasm and nucleolus; double-membraned nuclear envelope with pores; chromatin seen during interphase.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for each of three correct, paired points of difference, e.g. the centrosome – contains two cylindrical centrioles; each centriole has nine peripheral triplet fibrils; forms spindle apparatus in animal cells; the nucleus – contains nucleoplasm and nucleolus; double-membraned nuclear envelope with pores; chromatin seen during interphase.

items.stem:
(a) Distinguish between the ribosome and the mitochondrion on any three points. (3 marks)
(b) A cell organelle has these features: 70S in prokaryotes and 80S in eukaryotes. Identify the organelle – the ribosome or the mitochondrion? Justify your answer. (2 marks)
items.answer: (a) The ribosome: granular structure without a membrane; made of RNA and proteins; 70S in prokaryotes and 80S in eukaryotes. The mitochondrion: double membrane, inner one folded into cristae; matrix with circular DNA and 70S ribosomes; site of aerobic respiration. (b) The ribosome.
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark for each of three paired differences. (b) 1 mark: the ribosome; 1 mark: “70S in prokaryotes and 80S in eukaryotes” is a feature of the ribosome.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about the cell theory and prokaryotic cells is correct?
items.answer: Prokaryotic cells lack membrane-bound organelles.
items.markingKey: (b) Prokaryotic cells lack membrane-bound organelles. The other statements are false. Prokaryotic ribosomes are 70S, made of 50S and 30S subunits. Prokaryotes have a nucleoid without a nuclear membrane. Flagella are for motility; pili and fimbriae help in attachment.
options: Pili and fimbriae are the organs of locomotion of bacteria.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about the cell membrane, cell wall and endomembrane system is incorrect?
items.answer: Rough ER is the main site of lipid synthesis.
items.markingKey: (a) The incorrect statement is “Rough ER is the main site of lipid synthesis.” Correct form: Smooth ER synthesises lipids; rough ER, with ribosomes, synthesises and secretes proteins.
options: Rough ER is the main site of lipid synthesis.
The fluid nature of the membrane is important for cell growth, formation of intercellular junctions, secretion, endocytosis and cell division.
In plant cells the vacuole can occupy up to 90 per cent of the volume of the cell.
The smooth ER is the major site for lipid synthesis; in animal cells lipid-like steroidal hormones are synthesised there.

items.stem: Explain the term “glycocalyx”.
items.answer: The outermost layer of the bacterial cell envelope, which may be a loose slime layer or a thick, tough capsule.

items.stem: Which of the following is a double-membrane-bound organelle?
items.answer: chloroplast

items.answer: (i) The rough endoplasmic reticulum (ii) frequently observed in cells active in protein synthesis and secretion (iii) stacks of flat, disc-shaped cisternae; packages materials for intracellular targets or secretion

items.answer: Microbodies in germinating fatty seeds that convert fats into carbohydrates.

items.answer: The ribosome: granular structure without a membrane; site of protein synthesis. The nucleus: controls cell activities; chromatin seen during interphase.
